steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Fan in Service Diagnostics
steps.body: On fan-equipped models: DC fan runs during Service Diagnostics step 4. Skip if model has no fan.
steps.sourceExcerpt: On fan-equipped models: DC fan runs during Service Diagnostics step 4. Skip if model has no fan.

steps.title: Disconnect P14
steps.body: Power off. Unplug P14 from control.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Unplug P14 from control.

steps.title: Fan motor — P14 pins 1 & 2
steps.body: Ohms between P14-1 and P14-2. W11480208 spec 145–185 kΩ.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Ohms between P14-1 and P14-2. W11480208 spec 145–185 kΩ.

steps.title: Reconnect P14 and restore power
steps.body: Reconnect P14. Restore power.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect P14. Restore power.

steps.title: Continue after Service Diagnostics entry
steps.body: Service Diagnostics should be available (1-2-3 entry, press Key #2, close door to start). Continue with bench checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to Component Testing; use Service Diagnostics Cycle for live load verification.

steps.title: 13 VDC and fan spins in Service Diagnostics?
steps.body: During fan interval: 13 VDC ±5% at P14-1 and P14-2; fan spins.
steps.sourceExcerpt: During fan interval: 13 VDC ±5% at P14-1 and P14-2; fan spins.

steps.title: Replace fan assembly
steps.body: Replace DC fan motor assembly.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: Fan good but no DC drive — replace control.

steps.title: DC fan verified
steps.body: DC fan verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Diverter in Service Diagnostics
steps.body: Run Service Diagnostics — listen for spray zone changes or inspect diverter shaft rotation. Verify diverter disk installed.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Run Service Diagnostics — listen for spray zone changes or inspect diverter shaft rotation. Verify diverter disk installed.

steps.title: Disconnect P6
steps.body: Power off. Unplug P6 from control. Measure diverter motor at P6-4 and P6-6.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Unplug P6 from control. Measure diverter motor at P6-4 and P6-6.

steps.title: Diverter motor — P6 pins 4 & 6
steps.body: Ohms between P6-4 and P6-6. W11480208 spec 1100–1400 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Ohms between P6-4 and P6-6. W11480208 spec 1100–1400 Ω.

steps.title: Reconnect P6 and restore power
steps.body: Reconnect P6. Restore power.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect P6. Restore power.

steps.title: Continue after Service Diagnostics entry
steps.body: Service Diagnostics should be available (1-2-3 entry, press Key #2, close door to start). Continue with bench checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to Component Testing; use Service Diagnostics Cycle for live load verification.

steps.title: Diverter rotates in Service Diagnostics?
steps.body: 120 VAC at P6-4 and P6-6 during diverter interval; motor must be connected.
steps.sourceExcerpt: 120 VAC at P6-4 and P6-6 during diverter interval; motor must be connected.

steps.title: Replace diverter assembly
steps.body: Replace diverter motor assembly if open/out of range.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: Motor good but no AC output — replace control. If error persists, run diverter sensor test (W11633848).

steps.title: Diverter motor verified
steps.body: Diverter motor verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Mechanical door checks
steps.body: Verify installation/leveling, latch obstructions, door seal seated, and racks not interfering with door closure.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Verify installation/leveling, latch obstructions, door seal seated, and racks not interfering with door closure.

steps.title: Disconnect P12
steps.body: Power off. Remove outer door and toe panels. Verify P12 and door latch connectors seated. Disconnect P12 from control.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Remove outer door and toe panels. Verify P12 and door latch connectors seated. Disconnect P12 from control.

steps.title: Door closed — P12 pins 9 & 11
steps.body: Ohms across P12-9 and P12-11 with door closed and strike fully latched. Expect 3 Ω or less.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Ohms across P12-9 and P12-11 with door closed and strike fully latched. Expect 3 Ω or less.

steps.title: Door open — P12 pins 9 & 11
steps.body: With door open and strike removed from latch, expect infinite resistance (open circuit).
steps.sourceExcerpt: With door open and strike removed from latch, expect infinite resistance (open circuit).

steps.title: 13 VDC at P11-7 with door open?
steps.body: Reconnect P12. Power on, door open: red lead P11-7, black P10-2 (DC GND). Expect 13 VDC.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect P12. Power on, door open: red lead P11-7, black P10-2 (DC GND). Expect 13 VDC.

steps.title: Continue after Service Diagnostics entry
steps.body: Service Diagnostics should be available (1-2-3 entry, press Key #2, close door to start). Continue with bench checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to Component Testing; use Service Diagnostics Cycle for live load verification.

steps.title: Door switch OK in Service Diagnostics?
steps.body: Run Service Diagnostics cycle (Key #2 after entry). Verify door-open pause and close-resume behavior.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Run Service Diagnostics cycle (Key #2 after entry). Verify door-open pause and close-resume behavior.

steps.title: Repair door harness
steps.body: Repair loose connections or harness between door switch and P12.

steps.title: Replace door switch/latch
steps.body: Replace door switch/latch assembly and retest.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: Door switch and wiring good but control does not sense door — replace ACU.

steps.title: Door switch verified
steps.body: Door switch circuit verified — reassemble.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Drain path mechanical check
steps.body: Verify drain hose, disposal plug, check valve, filter. Run Service Diagnostics drain interval first.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Verify drain hose, disposal plug, check valve, filter. Run Service Diagnostics drain interval first.

steps.title: Disconnect P5
steps.body: Power off. Unplug P5 from control.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Unplug P5 from control.

steps.title: VSM drain motor — P5 pins 5 & 6
steps.body: Ohms P5-5 to P5-6. W11480208 VSM spec 41–51 Ω. (SSM drain: P5-3 & P5-4 — use w11633848-drain-motor.)
steps.sourceExcerpt: Ohms P5-5 to P5-6. W11480208 VSM spec 41–51 Ω. (SSM drain: P5-3 & P5-4 — use w11633848-drain-motor.)

steps.title: Reconnect P5 and restore power
steps.body: Reconnect P5. Restore power.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect P5. Restore power.

steps.title: Continue after Service Diagnostics entry
steps.body: Service Diagnostics should be available (1-2-3 entry, press Key #2, close door to start). Continue with bench checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to Component Testing; use Service Diagnostics Cycle for live load verification.

steps.title: Drain motor runs in Service Diagnostics?
steps.body: 120 VAC at P5-5 and P5-6 during drain interval (motor connected).
steps.sourceExcerpt: 120 VAC at P5-5 and P5-6 during drain interval (motor connected).

steps.title: Replace drain motor
steps.body: Replace drain pump if winding failed or impeller damaged.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: Motor good but no AC output — replace control.

steps.title: VSM drain motor verified
steps.body: VSM drain motor verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Disconnect P4
steps.body: Power off. Remove toe/access panels. Disconnect P4 from control.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Remove toe/access panels. Disconnect P4 from control.

steps.title: Heater — P4 pins 2 & 3
steps.body: Ohms between P4-2 and P4-3. W11480208 spec 10–40 Ω including element and hi-limit in circuit.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Ohms between P4-2 and P4-3. W11480208 spec 10–40 Ω including element and hi-limit in circuit.

steps.title: Isolate open heater path
steps.body: If open: check heater element and hi-limit thermostat continuity separately. Repair harness or replace open part.
steps.sourceExcerpt: If open: check heater element and hi-limit thermostat continuity separately. Repair harness or replace open part.

steps.title: Reconnect P4 and restore power
steps.body: Reconnect P4. Restore power.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect P4. Restore power.

steps.title: Continue after Service Diagnostics entry
steps.body: Service Diagnostics should be available (1-2-3 entry, press Key #2, close door to start). Continue with bench checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to Component Testing; use Service Diagnostics Cycle for live load verification.

steps.title: 120 VAC at heater during Service Diagnostics?
steps.body: Volts AC at P4-2 and P4-3 during heater interval.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Volts AC at P4-2 and P4-3 during heater interval.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: Heater circuit good but no AC output — replace control. If heat error persists, run OWI test (W11633848 procedure).

steps.title: Heater verified
steps.body: Heater element and drive verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Door-open LED check
steps.body: Open door — interior LED tubes should turn on for up to 10 minutes. Two LEDs wired in parallel; one can fail independently.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Open door — interior LED tubes should turn on for up to 10 minutes. Two LEDs wired in parallel; one can fail independently.

steps.title: Disconnect P9
steps.body: Power off. Remove toe and outer door panels. Verify P9 seated. Disconnect P9 from control.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Remove toe and outer door panels. Verify P9 seated. Disconnect P9 from control.

steps.title: Each LED passes diode check?
steps.body: Diode mode: numeric reading anode→cathode; OL cathode→anode on each LED tube.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Diode mode: numeric reading anode→cathode; OL cathode→anode on each LED tube.

steps.title: 13 VDC at P9-2 & P9-4 (door open, P9 unplugged)?
steps.body: Power on, door open within 10 min window: 13 VDC between P9-2 and P9-4 with lights disconnected.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power on, door open within 10 min window: 13 VDC between P9-2 and P9-4 with lights disconnected.

steps.title: Replace defective LED
steps.body: Replace failed LED tube individually and retest.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: LEDs good but no 13 V output — replace control.

steps.title: Interior LED verified
steps.body: Interior LED lighting verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Overfill prerequisites
steps.body: Inspect leak pan for water. Verify float moves freely. Empty pan if water present and find leak source before continuing.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect leak pan for water. Verify float moves freely. Empty pan if water present and find leak source before continuing.

steps.title: Disconnect P11
steps.body: Power off. Remove toe and outer door panels. Unplug P11 from control.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Remove toe and outer door panels. Unplug P11 from control.

steps.title: Float down — P11 pins 6 & 7
steps.body: Float in normal (down) position with assembly installed: ohms P11-6 to P11-7. Expect 3 Ω or less.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Float in normal (down) position with assembly installed: ohms P11-6 to P11-7. Expect 3 Ω or less.

steps.title: Float up — P11 pins 6 & 7
steps.body: Raise Styrofoam floater (up position): expect open circuit between P11-6 and P11-7.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Raise Styrofoam floater (up position): expect open circuit between P11-6 and P11-7.

steps.title: Continue after Service Diagnostics entry
steps.body: Service Diagnostics should be available (1-2-3 entry, press Key #2, close door to start). Continue with bench checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to Component Testing; use Service Diagnostics Cycle for live load verification.

steps.title: 13 VDC at P11-6 & P11-7 (P11 unplugged)?
steps.body: Power on with P11 disconnected from board. DC volts P11-6 to P11-7 — expect 13 VDC.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power on with P11 disconnected from board. DC volts P11-6 to P11-7 — expect 13 VDC.

steps.title: Repair float harness
steps.body: Repair harness or connections to overfill switch.

steps.title: Replace float assembly
steps.body: Replace overfill/float switch assembly.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: Float switch good but no 13 V supply — replace control.

steps.title: Overfill circuit verified
steps.body: Overfill float switch verified — reconnect P11 and retest.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Wash path prerequisites
steps.body: Inspect sump, coarse filter, spray arms. Run Service Diagnostics wash-motor interval first.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect sump, coarse filter, spray arms. Run Service Diagnostics wash-motor interval first.

steps.title: Disconnect P5
steps.body: Power off. Unplug P5 from control.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Unplug P5 from control.

steps.title: VSM wash motor — P5 pins 1 & 2
steps.body: Ohms P5-1 to P5-2. Variable-speed spec 16–18 Ω. (SSM models: 7–12 Ω — use w11633848-wash-motor.)
steps.sourceExcerpt: Ohms P5-1 to P5-2. Variable-speed spec 16–18 Ω. (SSM models: 7–12 Ω — use w11633848-wash-motor.)

steps.title: Reassemble and run Service Diagnostics
steps.body: Reconnect P5. Reassemble panels. Restore power and run Service Diagnostics to verify wash motor operation.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect P5. Reassemble panels. Restore power and run Service Diagnostics to verify wash motor operation.

steps.title: Replace wash motor
steps.body: Replace variable-speed wash motor if winding failed.

steps.title: VSM wash motor verified
steps.body: VSM wash motor ohms verified. No AC bench run test — motor uses DC drive from control.
